chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Abu al-Faraj al-Sandy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I was circumambulating with him around the House (Kaaba), so he said: 'Which of these is greatest in sanctity?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you are more knowing of this than I.' He repeated it to me, so I said to him, 'Entering the House.' He said: 'The Yamani corner is upon a door from the doors of Paradise, opened for the Shiah of the Progeny of Muhammad, closed off for others. And there is no believer who supplicates with a supplication at it, except that his supplication ascends until it adheres to the Throne, with no veil between it and Allah.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yamani Corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.شِيعَةِ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: The Shiah (Followers) of the Progeny of Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the Yamani corner of the Kaaba in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the Yamani corner (al-Rukn al-Yamani) as a unique spiritual gateway to Paradise, explicitly reserved for the Shiah of the Prophet's family. This distinction underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the special status of the Ahl al-Bayt's followers, where supplications made here ascend directly to the Divine Throne without any intervening veil, symbolizing unmediated closeness to God.
